Before building the descriptor RBF kernel, keep only the 60 standardized RDKit descriptors with the largest absolute Spearman correlation to the training target (computed on training molecules only), with gamma = 1/60 on the selected columns.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted answers. Only train_y is used, to build the ranking pairs, and test predictions are K_test @ alpha.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The new model is a pairwise-hinge ranking model on the same mixed kernel (Tanimoto plus RBF), fitted with L-BFGS. I checked the analytic gradient: the hinge part is K @ g_f with the coef sign handled correctly, and the regulariser part 2*lam*K@a is right because K is symmetric. Tied pairs are excluded, and pair sampling uses the seed argument. Memory and time look fine (about 15.5k pairs and n of about 776 per fold).

The numbers back the decision. The candidate's loss is 0.5957 against the incumbent's 0.4830, so it is about 0.113 worse. The difference is far beyond the noise, and rejecting it is right. A likely cause is that the hinge part is only a weak signal with lam=0.01 on an unnormalised kernel. Whatever the cause, it is a real result, not an artifact.

Recomputing z with one run each and noise sd 0.0070 gives z = (0.4830-0.5957)/(0.0070*sqrt(2)) ≈ -11.38. The harness reported -11.332. The small gap probably comes from a slightly different sd estimate or from how the values were adjusted, and it does not change the conclusion.
Each side has only one run. The gap is so large that this does not matter here.

description: Replace the SVR head with a kernel RankSVM model: f = K @ alpha, trained with a sampled pairwise hinge loss (about 20 pairs per molecule, seeded) plus 0.01 * alpha^T K alpha, minimized by L-BFGS with an analytic gradient, and predicted as K_test @ alpha.

Replace the single radius-2 Morgan Tanimoto kernel with the mean of Tanimoto kernels over radius 1, 2 and 3 fingerprints (2048 bits each), keeping the descriptor RBF kernel, the 0.5 mix, and the SVR and rank target unchanged.
Adds a Tanimoto kernel on RDKit path-based fingerprints (maxPath=6, 2048 bits) and averages it equally with the Morgan-Tanimoto and descriptor-RBF kernels, K = (K_morgan + K_desc + K_path) / 3.

Replace the SVR head with a Laplacian-regularized transductive solve: a 0.5 Tanimoto/descriptor-RBF kernel over train plus test molecules, a symmetric 7-NN graph with kernel-value weights, and f = (S + 0.5 L)^-1 S y, where test predictions are read from f.

Weight each standardized RDKit descriptor column by its absolute Spearman correlation with the rank-normalized training target (computed on the training fold, mean-normalized to 1, applied as sqrt(w) column scaling) and set the descriptor RBF gamma to 1/sum(w), leaving the Tanimoto kernel and 0.5/0.5 mix unchanged.

Append RDKit's 192-value CalcAUTOCORR2D autocorrelation descriptors (Moreau-Broto-type, Gasteiger-charge and atomic-property weighted) to the existing RDKit descriptor block so they pass through the unchanged constant-column filter, standardization, clipping and RBF descriptor kernel.

Adds a radius-2 2048-bit Morgan Tanimoto kernel on side-chain-only fragments (Murcko scaffold atoms removed via RWMol) and averages it equally with the full-molecule Tanimoto and descriptor RBF kernels, keeping the same SVR.

Replace the RBF descriptor kernel with a Laplacian kernel exp(-gamma * L1 distance) on the standardized descriptors, computed in row chunks, keeping the Tanimoto average, gamma=1/n_features, and SVR(C=5, epsilon=0.05).

Average three SVRs, each on the Morgan-Tanimoto/descriptor-RBF kernel mix but with the RDKit descriptors scaled differently (z-score with clipping, robust median/IQR, or rank-Gaussian fitted on the training fold), and average their test predictions after converting each to within-test ranks.

After the SVR predicts the test molecules, blend each prediction 0.7/0.3 with the mean prediction of its test-set neighbours (Tanimoto >= 0.5, diagonal excluded, row-normalized), leaving molecules with no neighbours unchanged; the training pipeline is untouched.

Weight each standardized RDKit descriptor by its absolute Spearman correlation with the training target (floored at 0.05, computed on the training fold only), scale the descriptor columns by these weights, and set the RBF gamma to 1/sum(w^2), leaving the Morgan-Tanimoto kernel and SVR settings unchanged.

Replace the z-score-and-clip step on the standardized RDKit descriptor matrix with a per-column normal-quantile transform fitted on the training fold (training ranks mapped via (rank-0.5)/n and norm.ppf; test values mapped by np.interp over the sorted training values), leaving the Morgan Tanimoto kernel, the gamma setting and the SVR unchanged.

issues: No sign of a measurement workaround. There is no file or network access, no pasted answers, and no use of test labels. The IDF is computed from the train and test fingerprints together, which uses the test SMILES but not their labels. fit_predict receives those SMILES as inputs, so this is legitimate transductive use. Still, it makes the predictions depend on what else is in the test batch, and the final scoring on held-out molecules will use a different test batch.

The Tanimoto change is correct. Once A = x*sqrt(idf), A@B.T gives the idf-weighted intersection. For binary fingerprints, the squared row sums give the idf-weighted bit counts. That makes the result a proper weighted Tanimoto. Without the squaring, the scaled vectors would give the wrong norms.

Not checked: the rest of train.py is not visible. If tanimoto is also called somewhere on unscaled inputs, or if the scaled X goes to a model that expects binary bits, this change also affects that path. That would not invalidate the result.

Recomputed z = (0.4830 - 0.4826) / (0.0070 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/1)) ≈ 0.04, which matches the reported 0.041. A gain of 0.0004 is well within the noise (sd 0.0070), so rejecting it is consistent with the numbers. The added code is also not justified by such a small gain.

description: Weight each radius-2 2048-bit Morgan bit by its transductive IDF (sqrt-scaled columns) so the Tanimoto kernel becomes IDF-weighted, keeping the 0.5/0.5 mix with the descriptor RBF kernel and the SVR head unchanged.

issues: Recomputed z is about 1.633 (candidate mean 0.4690 over 2 runs vs incumbent 0.4830 over 1 run, SE = 0.0070*sqrt(1/2+1/1) = 0.00857). This agrees with the harness value of 1.626 to within rounding.

description: Add an ARDRegression (default priors, max_iter=300) on the standardized, clipped RDKit descriptors, fit to the rank-normalized target, and output 0.7 times the SVR test-set rank plus 0.3 times the ARD test-set rank.

Replace the single C=5 SVR with an average of three SVRs (C in {1, 5, 20}, epsilon 0.05) on the same mixed kernel and rank target, averaging their within-test-set ranks before the existing ARD blend.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff only changes featurize(): Morgan bits now use custom atom invariants (atomic number*10 + degree). There is no file or network access, no pasted values and no use of test labels.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. Train and test molecules go through the same featurize. The custom invariants are a valid RDKit input, although they leave out charge, hydrogen count, ring membership and aromaticity. That loss of information is a likely reason the candidate scores worse.

Minor: the candidate uses the older GetMorganFingerprintAsBitVect API and converts bits with a Python list() call. This works but is slower and less clean than the generator it replaces, so it goes against 'simpler is better'.

My z: (0.4690 - 0.4860) / (0.0070*sqrt(1 + 1/2)) = -1.98, which matches the reported -1.976 apart from rounding of the inputs. The candidate is worse by about 0.017, so the reject decision is consistent with the numbers.

description: Reduce the Morgan atom invariants to atomic number and heavy-atom degree only (radius 2, 2048 bits, binary) via the legacy rdMolDescriptors Morgan function with a custom invariants list, leaving the rest of the Tanimoto/descriptor-RBF/SVR/ARD pipeline unchanged.
Adds a shrunken (0.5x) Ridge(alpha=30) correction, fit on standardized RDKit descriptors, to the SVR's in-sample residuals, leaving the kernel, SVR hyperparameters, and rank blend unchanged.

Grid-search SVR C in {1, 5, 20} and epsilon in {0.02, 0.05, 0.1} with a seeded 3-fold inner split scored by Spearman, then refit SVR on all training molecules with the best pair while keeping the mixed kernel and rank target unchanged.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The candidate reads no files, pastes in no answers and never touches test labels. brics_counts builds features from test_smiles only, the same way the incumbent already does for fingerprints and descriptors.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The BRICS fragment hash (character codes weighted by position, mod 1024) is deterministic, so features are the same on every run. The min-max kernel on non-negative counts is a valid kernel, and the denominator is clamped at 1e-9. BRICSDecompose always returns at least one fragment, so no molecule gets an all-zero row and the kernel diagonal stays 1.
Minor robustness note: if Chem.MolFromSmiles returns None, BRICSDecompose will crash. The incumbent's featurizers presumably parse the same SMILES, so this adds no new risk.

Cost looks fine. The minmax loop does about n_test+n_train row passes over arrays of about 776x1024, which is cheap. BRICS decomposition adds some per-fit time but should stay far below the 10-minute limit.
No job has run yet, so there are no numbers to check claims against and z cannot be computed.

description: Adds a third kernel, a min-max (generalized Jaccard) kernel on 1024-bin BRICS fragment count vectors (crc32-hashed), and averages it equally with the Morgan-Tanimoto and descriptor-RBF kernels before the same SVR; the ARD member is unchanged.

Replace the ARDRegression member with a linear pairwise logistic ranker (L2 lam=1e-2, L-BFGS-B with analytic gradient, up to 40000 seeded pairs with |y_i-y_j|>0.05) on the standardized clipped descriptors, keeping the 0.3 blend weight.

Add a sklearn GaussianProcessRegressor (ConstantKernel * ARD RBF plus WhiteKernel, fit on the 60 descriptors most Spearman-correlated with the rank-normalized target) and blend its rank predictions 0.3 with the SVR at 0.4 and ARD at 0.3.

The timeout comes from the Gaussian process: its 60-dimensional ARD RBF kernel has 61 hyperparameters, so each likelihood-gradient step is very costly on about 780 training points, repeated across 15 fits. Switching to a single shared length scale keeps the GP but makes each optimizer step far cheaper.

Replace the kernel ensemble with an average of 3 numpy message-passing networks (3 rounds of h <- tanh(W1 h + A h W2), hidden 32, sum-pooled readout) trained by full-batch Adam on the rank-normalized target with a hand-written backward pass.

issues: Candidate is far worse than incumbent (0.9525 vs 0.4690); Spearman ~0.05 is near-random, consistent with an undertrained small GNN (hidden 32, 150 full-batch steps, single model), not with a correctness bug.
Sum pooling makes the graph readout scale with molecule size, which likely hurts; weight decay is also applied to biases. Minor quality issues, not measurement-invalidating.
Harness z of -56.158 reproduces as |z| ~ 56.4 using sd 0.0070 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2); sign convention indicates worse-than-incumbent.

description: The job timed out because 15 fits each train 3 ensemble members for 300 full-batch epochs of a hand-written message-passing net over about 20k atoms, roughly 13,500 epochs of dense work in total. Cutting the ensemble to 1 member and the epochs to 150 cuts the compute about sixfold so the job fits within 600 s.

Before featurization, each SMILES is parsed, reduced to its largest fragment, and neutralized with RDKit's Uncharger (same preprocessing in featurize and descriptors), and the Morgan generator uses includeChirality=True (RDKit's keyword for useChirality), falling back to the raw string when parsing returns None.

Add 20 kernel-PCA coordinates (double-centred 0.5*(Tanimoto+descriptor-RBF) kernel, Nystrom projection for test) to the standardized descriptors, fit a small LightGBM on them, and blend its rank 0.4 with the SVR rank 0.4 and the ARD rank 0.2.

Appends 20 atom-level count features (a 10-bin Gasteiger partial-charge histogram and a 10-bin histogram of per-atom Crippen logP contributions, used in place of the ~70 Crippen atom-type counts because the type table is not accessible through the allowed API) to the RDKit descriptors before standardization, so they feed the descriptor RBF kernel and ARDRegression.

Replace the SVR head with five binary C-SVC ordinal thresholds (training quantiles 0.2 to 0.8, C=1) on the shared mixed Tanimoto/descriptor-RBF kernel, summing their decision values as the score in the unchanged 0.7/0.3 rank blend with ARD.

Adds a matched-pair difference model: a Ridge (alpha=10) on training-pair descriptor differences and Tanimoto similarity predicts y_i - y_j over each training molecule's 10 nearest neighbours above 0.5, test predictions are similarity-weighted neighbour values plus the ridge correction (falling back to SVR when no neighbour exceeds 0.5), and the result is blended at weight 0.3 with the existing SVR/ARD rank blend.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted answers. Test labels are never used. The WL vocabulary is built only from the training molecules, and test molecules are only mapped onto it, so nothing leaks.

Python's built-in hash() of strings is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the label IDs change from run to run. Train and test are hashed in the same process, so they stay consistent and the kernel does not change apart from vanishingly rare hash collisions. This is not a correctness problem, but hashlib or keeping the full string as the label would be cleaner and fully deterministic.
featurize() and tanimoto() look like dead code now, at least in this fit path. Remove them if nothing else uses them, to keep the script simple.

Dense WL count matrix: the vocabulary could reach tens of thousands of labels, about 776 x 2e4 float64, roughly 125 MB. That is well within 6 GB, and building the docs in pure Python should fit the 10-minute limit.
If a SMILES fails to parse (MolFromSmiles returns None), the script crashes. The incumbent likely has the same exposure, so this is not new.
There is no run yet, so there are no numbers to check claims against, and z cannot be recomputed.

description: Replace the Morgan Tanimoto kernel with a Weisfeiler-Lehman subtree count kernel (3 iterations, atom and bond labels, crc32 hashing, cosine-normalised), keeping the 0.5/0.5 mix with the descriptor RBF kernel, the SVR and the ARD unchanged.
Shrink each test molecule's blended rank score toward 0.5 by a factor set by its max Morgan-Tanimoto similarity to the training set, then re-rank the shrunken scores.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. Picking the kernel weight w and the noise s2 by marginal likelihood uses only the training kernel and the training targets. Test molecules enter only through Kt_test and Kd_test at prediction time, so no test labels are used.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The nugget s2 is at least 0.1, so K stays positive definite and best is never None in practice. The script would only crash if every Cholesky failed, and it does not guard against that.
Cosmetic: the SVR has been replaced by a GP / kernel ridge posterior mean, but the variable is still called svr_pred. Rename it if this is ever kept.

Numbers: the candidate scores 0.4799 against the incumbent mean of 0.4690, so it is 0.0109 worse. With noise sd 0.0070, the standard error of the difference is 0.0070*sqrt(1+1/2) ≈ 0.00857, giving z ≈ -1.27. That matches the harness value of -1.264 within rounding (sign convention: negative means worse). Rejecting is correct.
Extra cost for little gain: the change adds a 15-candidate grid of n×n Cholesky factorisations per fit, and the loss is worse. Under the simplicity rule, reject.

description: Choose the mixing weight w and noise level s2 of the Tanimoto/descriptor-RBF kernel by maximizing the GP log marginal likelihood over a 5x3 grid, then use the GP posterior mean in place of the SVR head before the existing ARD blend.

Adds a medoid-anchor embedding model: seeded k-means (k=64) on Morgan bits picks anchor medoids, molecules are embedded by standardized Tanimoto similarities to the anchors, and an RBF kernel ridge with median-distance bandwidth is rank-averaged with the existing blend at weight 0.25.

Two-round train-only self-distillation of the Tanimoto/descriptor-kernel SVR, using seeded 5-fold out-of-fold soft targets (0.5 and 0.3 label weights) before a final SVR fit that feeds the rank blend with ARD.

Greedy Caruana ensemble selection: a pool of five rank predictors (Tanimoto SVR, Tanimoto/descriptor-RBF SVR, ARDRegression, LightGBM on Morgan bits, Ridge on descriptors) is scored on a seeded 80/20 split of the training fold, up to 10 greedy with-replacement steps maximise Spearman of the rank average, then the chosen weights are applied to members refit on the full fold.

Append five ring-system and scaffold count features (ring-system count, rings in the largest system, generic-scaffold indicator, aromatic ring-atom count, ring-atom heavy-atom fraction) to the descriptor matrix before the keep/standardize step.

Adds out-of-fold, Bayesian-shrunk (m=5) target encodings of Morgan bits and BRICS fragments, summarized per molecule as mean/max/min, as extra columns for the ARD model while leaving the SVR unchanged.

Replace the global-gamma descriptor RBF with a self-tuning kernel exp(-||d_i-d_j||^2 / (2 sigma_i sigma_j)), where sigma is the distance to the 7th nearest training neighbour (train points exclude self; test points use the 7th nearest training molecule), keeping the 0.5/0.5 Tanimoto mix and SVR settings.

Add a third rank-blend member, an ElasticNetCV (l1_ratio in {0.1, 0.5, 0.9}, 5 inner folds, max_iter=5000) fit on the standardized clipped RDKit descriptors plus the 2048 Morgan bits to the rank-normalized target, with blend weights SVR 0.6, ARD 0.2, elastic net 0.2.

issues: No sign that the measurement is being worked around. The new ElasticNetCV is fit only on the training features and labels (D, y) and predicts on the test features (Dt). It does not touch any files, the network or the test labels.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. ElasticNetCV takes random_state=seed. Blending rank-normalized predictions is valid because the loss uses Spearman correlation. The new weights (0.6, 0.2, 0.2) sum to 1.

The claims match the numbers. The candidate's 0.4721 is 0.0031 worse than the incumbent's 0.4690. Recomputed z = -0.0031 / (0.0070 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2)) ≈ -0.36, which matches the harness value of -0.358 apart from rounding. This is well within noise, so reject stands.

Minor point: ElasticNetCV runs an internal 5-fold CV over 3 l1_ratio values. That adds runtime and code for no measured gain, so it goes against the 'simpler is better' rule even if a replicate came out neutral.

description: The job timed out because ElasticNetCV was fit on about 2,250 dense features (200 descriptors plus 2,048 Morgan bits) with 5-fold CV over 3 l1_ratios and max_iter=5000, so I fixed it by fitting it on the descriptor block only.

Replace the Morgan Tanimoto term with a histogram-intersection kernel on shortest-path atom-pair count vectors (element pairs by topological distance capped at 10, plus element and aromaticity counts), L1-normalized and averaged 0.5/0.5 with the descriptor RBF kernel.
Drop Morgan bits set in fewer than 2 or more than 98 percent of training molecules, applying the same column mask to the test features before the Tanimoto kernel.
Reweight the Morgan bits by the absolute coefficients of a seeded, inner-CV-tuned ridge fit to the rank target, and use the weighted Tanimoto kernel in the 0.5/0.5 mix.
Abort: N_TREES is defined in train.py but never used, since the current model is an SVR plus ARDRegression with no random forest, so raising it to 1000 would change nothing.

Turn on chirality in the Morgan generator (radius 2, 2048 bits) and encode ring membership by setting each atom's isotope label to 1 if it is in a ring and 0 otherwise, since the isotope is part of the default Morgan atom invariants; the Tanimoto/descriptor-RBF kernel mix and everything else stay unchanged.

Adds a SMILES character n-gram (n=2 to 4) count kernel, cosine-normalized over canonical SMILES with a vocabulary fitted on train+test strings, and averages it equally with the Tanimoto and descriptor-RBF kernels before the unchanged SVR.

Adds a min-max kernel on folded 2048-bin radius-2 Morgan count vectors divided by each molecule's heavy-atom count, averaged equally with the existing binary Tanimoto and descriptor-RBF kernels for the SVR, with the other two kernels unchanged.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The PLS projection is fit on the training fold only (train X and rank-transformed train y). The test molecules are only passed through transform, and no test labels are used. There is no file or network access and no pasted values.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The PLS scores are standardized with training-fold statistics only. The three kernels are averaged, so K_train stays positive semi-definite. K_test has the shape (n_test, n_train) that SVR(kernel='precomputed') expects.

Likely reason for the regression: the PLS kernel is built from labels. On the training fold it lines up with y by construction, so it overfits there and does not carry over to unseen scaffolds. It also reduces the weight of the Tanimoto and descriptor kernels from 1/2 each to 1/3 each.

The z value checks out. Difference = 0.5281 - 0.4690 = 0.0591. SE = 0.0070*sqrt(1 + 1/2) ≈ 0.00857, so |z| ≈ 6.89. The harness reports -6.867, which matches up to rounding. Here the negative sign means the candidate is worse. Rejecting it is correct: the loss rose by about 0.059, far beyond the noise.

description: Add a third kernel to the SVR: an RBF on 8 standardized PLS scores (fit on training Morgan bits against the rank-normalized target, training data only), averaged equally with the Tanimoto and descriptor-RBF kernels.

Append the ErG reduced-graph fingerprint and the 42 MQN counts, standardized on training statistics and clipped to ±5, to the standardized RDKit descriptor matrix used only by the RBF kernel, leaving the Tanimoto term, kernel mix, SVR, and ARD member unchanged.

Replace the SVR head with Huber-loss kernel ridge fitted by 10 IRLS iterations (lam=0.3, delta=0.2 in standardized rank-target units) on the same combined Tanimoto/descriptor-RBF kernel, keeping the ARD member and the 0.7/0.3 rank blend unchanged.

Average three binary Tanimoto kernels built from unfolded radius-2 Morgan IDs folded to 1024, 2048 and 4096 bits, then mix with the descriptor RBF kernel 0.5/0.5, keeping the SVR and ARD members unchanged.

Before building the descriptor RBF kernel and the ARD member, keep only the standardized RDKit descriptors that appear in the top 25 by absolute Spearman correlation with the rank-normalized target in at least 60% of 50 seeded 70% training subsamples, with gamma set from the kept count.
